system.summary: Lasry's 'TNA SP 106' key (Sept 1645): a numerical homophonic alphabet of one- and two-digit values (up to five for E and I) with a nomenclator of three-digit numbers (124 England?, 126 the King, 127 the Queen, 279 and ...), numbers separated by colons.
system.sibling_key: Same key, per Lasry's files, on the sibling records R752 (ff. 207-210), R754 (ff. 211-212) and R788 (ff. 218, 220-221; f. 219 is in SP106-2)
system.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from the former hm1645, which joined six letters in four of Lasry's keys. This entry keeps the TNA SP 106 key only. Lasry's key file says there are no nulls; the figures 16, 30, 39, 49, 59, 77, 78, 79, which the key leaves without a value, fall between words in the letters, so nulls are left 'unknown' here. The other keys have their own entries: sp106r787 (SP106-2), sp106r924 (SP106-8), sp106r929 (SP106-5).

prior_solution.where: DECODE record files of R785, R790, R923 (George Lasry, 23 Oct 2020: reconstructed key, interlinear plaintext, dating notes)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: apply_key.py (key applied group by group to the transcription and compared with Lasry's plaintext)

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE record pages with the shared cookie; each links Lasry's reconstructed key and plaintext (2020-10-23) for the ff. 207-247 run. R785, R790 and R923 carry his 'TNA SP 106' key and the interlinear file for ff. 207-234.

Re-fetched the record files and applied Lasry's TNA SP 106 key group by group to the transcriptions of R785, R790 and R923 (apply_key.py). The key gives a value to 3069 of 3373 groups; on the lines whose columns line up in his interlinear file (2712 keyed groups) every value equals his plaintext.

Split from the former combined target hm1645 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R785, R790, R923 (TNA SP 106 key) stay here; R787 (SP106-2), R924 (SP106-8) and R929 (SP106-5) became sp106r787, sp106r924, sp106r929. Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; earlier steps are kept as recorded.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcriptions (Pettersson) and decryptions (Lasry) linked on DECODE R785, R790, R923; the files stay git-ignored in decode/ as DECODE's and Lasry's work.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): Lasry's plaintexts of R785, R790, R923 are on DECODE only (git-ignored copies no longer in any checkout); nothing could be read. All three relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved kept (Lasry's published decipherment); fraction_read 0.9099 -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b14): every file on R785, R790, R923 fetched with the shared DECODE cookie into the session scratchpad (b14_fetch.py): Pettersson's transcriptions, Lasry's key, interlinear and plaintext files, 7 page images. No contemporary decipherment, gloss or clear copy on the records.

Key decode of every cipher line (b14_hm.py) beside Lasry's plaintext, including the 17 lines apply_key.py skipped. Two key values corrected because every occurrence needs it: 292 = by (Lasry: because, 12 occurrences) and 435 = next (Lasry: of, 2).

The groups from 279 up form an alphabetical codebook (279 and ... 555 you); band plus contexts in the six letters of the key (including Lasry's French sections) fix 31 open groups: 295 business, 330 dispatch, 340 foot, 405 master, 446 particular, 502 she, 518 those, 548 who, 392+498 lord+ship, 475 religion, 476 rebel ... (texts/hm1645_codes.tsv); single-context values marked [?]. 541 (four contexts) does not resolve to one word.

Figures checked on the images where decode and sense disagreed: R785 'pertectly' is the writer's 10; R923 126 is 127 (7 over 6: the Queen); R923 554 your (4 over 5); R923 341 r a 382 497 = 'forrain [succour]', not Lasry's 'Lorrain support'. Other one-figure slips listed, not checked (texts/hm1645_corrections.tsv).

Readings written (texts/R785/R790/R923_reading.md, _en.md), aligned letter by letter with the decode (0.978, 0.980, 0.959 carried; b14_align.py); clean-sentence share on the bodies 0.841, 0.792, 0.84 (0.73, 0.54, 0.56 with the figures' own spellings, which the lexicon does not know). All three set read.

Coordinator's correction: the three readings rewritten in the figures' own spelling (one-figure slips as written), the modern-spelling text kept only as the _en.md files. Re-aligned with the decode: 0.992, 0.995, 0.984 of each reading carried; clean-sentence share on the bodies 0.645, 0.542, 0.52 (modern spelling 0.841, 0.792, 0.84): the drop is the modern word list's artefact on period spellings; all three kept read.

outcome.method_basis: The three letters were taken from George Lasry's plaintext on the DECODE records (23 Oct 2020); his TNA SP 106 key, applied here to the transcriptions only as a check, reproduces it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit, 22 Oct 2026: none of the three letters' text is in the repository (Lasry's files were git-ignored and are no longer in any checkout), so no tokens are in a document that reads here. The earlier 0.9099 (apply_key.py: 3,069 of 3,373 groups with a value in Lasry's key, 14 Oct 2026) is withdrawn as a reading figure. 22 Oct 2026, re-read (b14): R785 (1,882 tokens), R790 (769), R923 (722) now read from the key decode (texts/*_reading.md), so 3,373 of 3,373 cipher tokens (docs/_check_profile.py --measure on the cipher lines of Lasry's interlinear file) are in documents that read = 1.0.

gaps.detail: Names or words seen once or twice in the six letters of the key, with no context that fixes them (541's four contexts need different words). 31 others were fixed from the codebook's alphabetical bands and context (texts/hm1645_codes.tsv).

gaps.item: one- and two-digit figures with no value in the key (78, 77, 16, 49, 59, 39, 30, 79 and three rarer ones: 11 distinct, 205 tokens)
gaps.detail: They fall between words throughout and are read as separators; whether the writer meant them as nulls (Lasry's key file says there are none) is not settled by anything on the records.

outcome.notes: Nothing about the text is new: Lasry's decipherment on DECODE is the reading. The writers sign with numbers (120 in R785 and R923). Siblings in the same key, per Lasry's files: R752, R754, R788 (ff. 218, 220-221). 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: no text of the three letters is in the repository; all three decoded, not read. Class kept: Lasry's decipherment exists on DECODE (2020). 22 Oct 2026, re-read (b14): the three letters read from the key decode with Lasry's key, two key corrections (292 = by, 435 = next) and 31 nomenclator values proposed from the codebook's alphabetical bands (texts/hm1645_codes.tsv); R785 is signed A. Cowley; R923's 'Lorrain support' is 'forrain [succour]'.

texts.label: R785, St Germain, 1 Sept 1645 (ff. 213-215)
texts.summary: A letter from Henrietta Maria's household at St Germain to Charles I, 1 September 1645, signed '120', reporting that the Queen is perfectly recovered; in English, in the 'TNA SP 106' cipher whose key and plaintext George Lasry reconstructed (DECODE, 2020).

reading_review.note: Read 22 Oct 2026 (b14) from the key decode of the DECODE transcription with Lasry's TNA SP 106 key (his plaintext D3061 compared line by line), two key corrections (292 = by, 435 = next) and nomenclator values proposed from the codebook's alphabetical bands (texts/hm1645_codes.tsv). The reading keeps the figures' own spelling (lettre, answear, termes, takeing; one-figure slips as written, listed in texts/hm1645_corrections.tsv); the _en.md file is the same text in modern spelling, holes kept. Aligned letter by letter with the decode (b14_align.py): 0.992 of the reading carried (0.978 for the earlier modern-spelling draft). _check_reading.py on the body 0.645 (40/62); the misses are mostly the period spellings, which the modern word list does not hold (the same text in modern spelling scored 0.841): an artefact of the word list, not holes in the sense, so kept read. Signed A. Cowley; image 3 (f. 215) is a second letter in the same key. Open: 15 code groups (22 tokens), mostly names.

texts.summary: A letter from Henrietta Maria's household at St Germains to Charles I, 29 September 1645, signed '120', on the Duke of Lorraine's 'little remote hopes'; in English, in Lasry's 'TNA SP 106' key.

reading_review.note: Read 22 Oct 2026 (b14) as for R785 (Lasry's plaintext D3070 compared); 126 corrected to 127 (the Queen) and 'forrain [?succour]' (not Lasry's 'Lorrain support') checked on the image. The reading keeps the figures' own spelling (lettre, answear, termes, takeing; one-figure slips as written, listed in texts/hm1645_corrections.tsv); the _en.md file is the same text in modern spelling, holes kept. Aligned 0.984 carried (0.959 for the modern-spelling draft; the rest is the 126/127 correction, the dates and Lasry's key list appended to the file); _check_reading.py on the body 0.52 (13/25), against 0.84 in modern spelling: the modern word list's artefact on releef, battail, avoyded, comeing, not holes in the sense, so kept read.
